page: Google Cloud Platform c4a-highmem-1 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance based on the arm64 architecture. Powered by a single dedicated ARMv8 Neoverse-V2 physical core running at 3.0 GHz, this server features 1 vCPU and 8.0 GB of system memory. The processor includes 64 KB of L1d cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 80 MB of L3 cache, with hardware-accelerated AES cryptography support. It does not include local NVMe storage or bundled GPUs.

Performance benchmarks reveal strong single-threaded capabilities alongside expected multi-core and bandwidth limitations. The instance achieves strong results in single-threaded compression and decompression, with gzip compression reaching 32.1 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 14.05 GB/sec. Geekbench single-core and text processing scores sit in the average tier, while multi-core benchmarks, software compilation, and ray tracing register in the lower performance brackets due to the single-vCPU constraint. Memory bandwidth is moderate, with read-only large block speeds at 29.49 GB/sec and write speeds at 11.76 GB/sec.

From a resource density perspective, the c4a-highmem-1 offers a cost-efficient entry point for memory-intensive workloads that do not require high parallel processing power. The 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio provides ample memory headroom for a single core. This configuration is suited for lightweight single-threaded applications, basic text processing, small-scale caching, or memory-bound utility scripts that benefit from a dedicated ARM core without the overhead of multi-core licensing.
